Comparative history · from Hammurabi to the present

Slavery, a history shared by every civilization

Mesopotamia, Rome, China, Korea, the caliphates, African kingdoms, the Ottoman Empire, the Crimean Tatars, the Barbary corsairs, the Aztecs, the European powers: nearly every major society has practiced slavery. This site sets these systems side by side, with their numbers, their rules and how they ended, so that anyone can compare them on the evidence.

12.5 MTransatlantic slave tradeAfricans embarked from 1501 to 1875, including 1.38 M under the French flag (SlaveVoyages database).
8 to 17 MOriental slave tradesSahara, Red Sea, Indian Ocean, from about 650 to 1900. Highly uncertain estimates (Alencastro, Austen).
2 to 5 MCrimean Tatar raidsCaptives taken in Poland-Lithuania and Muscovy, 1441-1774 (İnalcık, Charnysh and Lall).
1981Last abolitionMauritania, by decree; slavery was not made a criminal offense there until 2007. Saudi Arabia and Yemen: 1962.

By civilization

How this site compares

Criterion by criterion

Volume, duration, share of the population, legal status, hereditary transmission, manumission, end. No single criterion is enough to rank a system.

Figures that don't add up

A flow over three centuries, a stock on a given day and a share of the population are three different measures. Every figure says which one it is.

Every estimate attributed

Ranges are credited to the historian who proposes them, and disputed figures are flagged as such.
